A task owns nothing, so there is nothing to disclose and
no cascade to approve. There is no in-app undo;
Content and placement are separate concerns, and the
board is neither: a task stays on the board it was created
Priority changes only while the task is in the Backlog.
Work in motion is sent back there first, which re-opens its
Declining is a legitimate answer. The activity stays
InProgress and is closed by hand on the Course page.
The strip holds every board and the focus orders it. An
out-of-focus activity-based project is one entry, opening
to its activities on demand. Where the date has no focus,
the first board in the strip is the one named.
A board with no tasks is an empty board, not an empty
page. A project's template governs its boards; the
Chores board owns its template itself. The flag on an
unfinished predecessor names it and clears itself when
Every form on this surface drafts as it is filled in, so
leaving it half-finished, a crash and a restart all cost
nothing. The draft is one-way: nothing waits for it to be
kept. Whichever write commits the form discards it.
One request moves a task between columns and sends
it back to the Backlog alike. A task never moves to
another board. Returning it to the Backlog re-opens its
Triage happens at intake, so priority lives in the Backlog.
The buckets are Important and Urgent, Not Important
and Urgent, and Important and Not Urgent.
This is one of the three acts that archive a task, and the
one that takes a single card. A routine's task archives by
these same acts and no others.
A task owns nothing, so nothing goes with it.
